name: Shesepankh
desc: One of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, Saint Shesepankh, the Most-Holy. Shesepankh is an intelligent construct fashioned by King Deshret Al-Ahmar, who entrusted him with the duty of overseeing all the Jinn of the world. Shesepankh possesses a will of his own. Following the passing of King Deshret Al-Ahmar, he ceased his own functions and fell into stillness.

customize.name: Al-Ahmar
customize.desc: The ruler of the Sumeru desert. He is also known as King Deshret, Amun, and Scarlet King.

customize.name: Bennu
customize.desc: One of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, Saint Bennu, the Most-Radiant. Bennu is an intelligent construct fashioned by King Deshret, who entrusted him with the duty of guarding the gates of Aaru. He possesses a will of his own. He watches over the eternal utopia within Aaru — the Golden Slumber. Following the passing of King Deshret, he ceased his own functions and fell into stillness. Despite being an intelligent construct, Bennu possesses a remarkably vivid personality. Serious and earnest, he detests having his plans disrupted, and has little tolerance for irresponsible colleagues.

customize.name: Hermanubis
customize.desc: One of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, Saint Hermanubis, the Greatest of Sages. The only one among the Seven Pillars to ascend from humanity to the rank of a god's familiar. Born of the Tighnar people, he was a sage and warrior known far and wide. Sincere, steadfast, kind, and steady, he earned widespread respect. He was the guide of all priests, and within the academic world, he is honored as a foundational figure of desert civilization.

customize.name: Jinn
customize.desc: Familiars of the Goddess of Flowers, birthed from intoxicating dreams and the bitter memories of loss.

customize.name: Nabu Malikata
customize.desc: The Goddess of Flowers, a friend of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and King Deshret.

customize.text: 's death, Al-Ahmar tricked the Jinn into serving him, and Shesepankh began to rule over all the Jinn in the world. In times past, he would often wander the desert in his spare time, asking travelers all manner of questions. Driven by a profound curiosity, he will tirelessly pursue any matter that piques his interest to its very heart. Looking back, this was perhaps because he oversaw the Jinn, whose mother was Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, an angel of wisdom who delighted in posing questions. Through what the Jinn relayed to him, Shesepankh too developed a fondness for inquiry. He believes that maintaining a leisurely air is a good thing, a piece of worldly wisdom for navigating life.

customize.name: Dehya
customize.desc: A member of the Eremites, a mercenary organization that roams the sands of Sumeru. Valiant and powerful, she enjoys great fame amongst her fellow Eremites.

customize.text: The Eremite wears armor with the image of Shesepankh, so he can contact her and give her strength.
